newsitem.title: UK: BBC promises to deliver for UK licence payers.
newsitem.headline: BBC promises to deliver for UK licence payers.

text.p: The BBC published a 50-page document on Tuesday in which it promised to deliver quality services and high standards for viewers and listeners.

"For a long time we took the relationship with the licence payer for granted," BBC chairman Sir Christopher Bland told a news conference. "This is a genuine attempt to make our services more accountable," he added.

The "BBC Statement of Promises to Viewers and Listeners' spells out some 250 aims covering the BBC's national, regional and local services. It will serve as a yardstick for the BBC's board of governors to measure the corporation's performance.
The final page of the document provides a list of phone numbers and addresses for viewers and listeners who want to voice complaints. However, the document is not legally binding.
"This wouldn't have the legal validity of a contract. It's a contract with a small "c' but we take these promises seriously," said Bland.

The five key promises are to provide something for everyone; to be fair, accurate and impartial; to provide value for money; to improve people's access to services; and to be accountable and responsible.
The BBC receives some 1.8 billion stg annually from the licence fee payable by all television set owners.
The fee is 89.50 stg for a colour set but the BBC is campaigning for an above inflation increase in order to maintain the strength of its services in the multi-channel digital age.
However, politicians are reluctant to sanction an increase and the BBC is under pressure to boost its income from commercial activities.
